title: Auto Captions Got a Name Wrong? Correct It Before Export
description: When auto captions get a name wrong, correct the transcript against the audio and verify every occurrence before exporting.
direct: When auto captions get a name wrong, correct the transcript against the audio and verify every occurrence before exporting. An automatic cleanup pass may improve punctuation while still guessing the wrong spelling.

cards.choice.heading: Prepare a short reference
cards.choice.body: Write down the intended spelling of people, products and specialist terms. Listen to ambiguous passages rather than changing them from context alone. If the speaker’s words are unclear, confirm them with the source instead of confidently inventing text.
sections.explain.heading: Review optional AI changes
sections.explain.body: AI Correct can help with typos and punctuation, but an unfamiliar name still needs human checking. The optional online text tools use the internet after consent. Core caption generation can run on device without uploading the video. Do not assume that automated text cleanup verifies identities.
sections.practice.heading: Inspect the delivery copy
sections.practice.body: Space Sheep Studio develops Just Captions for iPhone. Free single-video exports include a Just Captions watermark; Pro removes it and unlocks additional features. The app also exports SRT when separate timed text is needed. If a wrong name has already been burned into a video, edit the project and export another copy; simply editing a separate SRT will not change those existing video pixels. No perfect transcription accuracy is promised.

related.related.label: Related practical guide
steps.step-1.text: Import the spoken clip into Subtitle Maker: Just Captions and generate captions. Review names and numbers before choosing a style.
steps.step-2.text: Edit incorrect transcript words and check repeated occurrences individually. Replay the surrounding phrase to check meaning and timing.
steps.step-3.text: Export a captioned MP4 or MOV, then watch the saved file outside the editor. Keep the editable transcript if you will need revisions.
